mechanism_narrative: The sharp drop in WORKPLACES mobility over the last two weeks reduces weekday downtown footfall and spillover shopping demand, so RETAIL_REC should fall over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -21.7 to -50.1 across the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days while WORKPLACES remains near or below the current level.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility stays elevated while TRANSIT remains deeply suppressed, households are substituting home-based routines for discretionary trips, which lowers RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -45 and RESIDENTIAL rises above +4
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose to 5.0 while TRANSIT fell to -47.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days after TRANSIT is below -45 and RESIDENTIAL is above +4.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in GROCERY_PHARM signals fewer combined shopping-and-leisure trips to retail districts, and that substitution will pull RETAIL_REC down over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls by more than 5 points week-on-week from a negative level
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved from -19.9 to -27.1 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or remains flat in the week after a >5-point weekly drop in GROCERY_PHARM.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility surges while retail categories stay weak, leisure demand shifts outdoors rather than to shops, so RETAIL_REC declines over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above +50 after being below +40 the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumped to 58.0 while RETAIL_REC fell to -33.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not underperform its prior 28-day mean in the four weeks after PARKS exceeds +50.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized decline in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates broad access or attendance constraints; that combined shock reduces retail trips and pushes RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both reached their lowest snapshot values at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not below its last-28-day average when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain near current lows.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL both rise together, households are consolidating trips near home, which crowds out discretionary retail visits and lowers RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL both increase week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM declined to -27.1 while RESIDENTIAL rose to 5.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to decline within 14 days after simultaneous increases in GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent recovery in TRANSIT from its current trough will restore access to shopping areas and lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 5 points from a level below -40
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved marginally earlier then fell to -47.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to its prior 28-day mean after TRANSIT rises from below -40 by at least 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: In a restriction-tightening regime, a simultaneous drop in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT predicts a delayed retail contraction because commuting-linked purchases disappear before leisure spending fully adjusts.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -45 while TRANSIT stays below -45
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell to -50.1 and TRANSIT to -47.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within 7 days after WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are both below -45.
